Liaotang Weiyi contrasts speech that adequately expresses the way with speech that only expresses things. Drawing once with his whisk, he says the extreme of way and things is cut off in that single stroke, then gives the Chu king's city and the Ru River flowing east. Senses.Explanation: Startling heaven and shaking earth: Chan speakers use this heightened phrase for a word or movement with extraordinary force. Baichi Xingyuan says a fitting response would show great use and shake heaven and earth. Lianfeng Su gives the phrase as his answer when asked about the Linji school. Yuanwu Keqin says Cuiyan's end-of-summer address was stark enough to startle heaven and earth. Zhe'an Jingfan says a word flowing from one's own confidence could do the same, but then warns that the stage reached is perilous. Konggu Daocheng calls for a turn from the staff that would shake heaven and earth rather than a claim supported by charms. Liao'an Qingyu says an earlier master's words had such force even through illness. Yinyuan Longqi portrays the elder Baizhang's presence on the whisk as startling heaven and earth during a memorial address.

Senses.PreferredTarget: It takes a keen adept to startle the crowd; only a lion's cub can meet a strong opponent.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問：「虎以肉為生，因甚不食其子？」師云：「金不博金。」云：「魚以水為命，因甚死在水中？」師云：「伸腳原在縮腳裏。」云：「是法平等，無有高下，因甚觀音坐，善財立？」師云：「是法平等，無有高下。」云：「因甚觀音坐，善財立聻？」師云：「問事即得。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB386.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuan’an Feng. In Yuan'an Liao's record, an unnamed monk first asks why a tiger lives on meat but does not eat its own young. After the reply 'gold does not trade for gold,' the monk asks why fish live by water yet die in it. Yuan'an answers that stretching out the legs is originally within drawing them in. The monk then turns to equality of teaching and the unequal postures of seated Guanyin and standing Sudhana. The fish question is one of a sequence of contrasts; the reply does not offer a biological cause of death, but sets the opposed movements of extending and withdrawing together. The headword is rendered: Fish depend on water for life; why do they die in the water?

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB430.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Qibaifu of Yuquan. Qibai Defu's record supplies the sight of a dead fish floating on the water. An unnamed monk asks the fish-and-water question, and Qibai says that this was originally its place to settle. The monk shouts; Qibai slaps him and says, 'Alive.' The last word follows the monk's shout and the slap, not a report of the fish reviving. The encounter moves from the floating dead fish to a present exchange in which a voice and a blow answer each other. That sequence is essential to understanding why the familiar question is used here. The headword is rendered: Fish depend on water for life; why do they die in the water?

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問：「魚以水為命，因甚死在水中？」師云：「生也在水中，死也在水中。」進云：「還有透脫一路麼？」師云：「有。」進云：「如何是透脫一路？」師云：「一串穿卻。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J40/J40nB477.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tianyixiang. An unnamed monk asks Tianyi Juxiang the same question. Tianyi answers that birth is in the water and death is in the water. The monk then asks whether there is a way through and out; Tianyi says yes, but answers the request to identify it with 'run one string through it all.' The reply does not name a second location outside the water. It brings the proposed escape back to the birth-and-death pair in the question, without supplying a literal account of how a fish can avoid dying. The headword is rendered: Fish depend on water for life; why do they die in the water?

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 下一狐疑了一狐疑？汝等諸人不妨於魯公亭上、烈女橋邊東󳬇西󳬇，忽然於出水、未出水時領略得去，要見智門則易，要見東湖則難，何故？芰荷風何止十里在？舉雲門問僧：今夏做箇什麼？僧云：和尚寔問，某甲即道。門云：倣賊人心虗。師拈云：雲門問處既不實，者僧答處痴裏放奸。若是薦福，一棒一條痕。何故？山僧從來不使虗頭。結夏，上堂。諸方開烹金爐，布漫天網，盡法無民。薦福門下，飢噇飯，熱乘凉，一任諸人。何故？深水得魚渾信僉，不曾將酒祭江神。上堂。塵塵爾，念念爾，法法爾。燕語鶯啼，驢鳴犬吠。不是，不是。召眾云：鄱陽湖夜來洪水泛漲，浸了三州六縣多少民地。上堂：不是而上事，亦非格外機。蚯蚓抹過東海，蝍蟟吞却須彌，木人撫掌笑揚扇。上堂。參禪須參活句。召眾云：天下老骨橫說竪說是死句，六代祖師直指曲指是死句，五千四十八卷金口所宣是死句。畢竟如何是活句？良久，下座。上堂，舉達磨見武帝公案，師頌云：波斯手裏捻生銕，把作希奇無價珍，識破分文元不直，寒光笑袞浪花新。上堂。魚行水濁，鳥飛毛落。召眾云：若起一毫佛見法見，盡六州之鐵難鑄錯。上堂，舉：石梯一日侍者請浴，梯云：既不洗塵，亦不洗垢，浴作什麼？侍者云：和尚先去，某甲將皂角後來。梯乃笑，師云：侍者大似恭而無禮。上堂：凡所見色，皆是見心。心不自心，因色故有。師拈云：馬大師認奴作郎。上堂，舉：僧問馬祖和尚：離四句，絕百非，請師直指西來意。祖云：我今日無心情。問取智藏，藏云：我今日頭痛，不能為汝說。問取海兄，海云：我到者裏却不會。復舉似祖，祖云：藏頭白，海頭黑。師云：馬大師如王小波，合成羣隊，巧同計較。這僧不躍禹門三級浪，勞勞只麼袞春風。上堂。一大藏教是箇切脚，切謂古德是大妄語。近因披閱，仔細撿點，將來是真語者，試將切脚切出一字，直是親切，不同泛常。今日舉皷，煩主丈子普告大眾。以丈卓一下，下座。上堂：謝一書記，的的西來意，一字不著畫。置之太虗而不見其寬，置之針孔而不見其窄。端的有誰見得親？木人眼光如電掣。上堂，舉：僧問智門：如何是佛？門云：踏破草鞋赤脚走。僧問：如何是佛向上事？門云：主丈頭上挑日月。師云：大小智門答者僧所問，大似臘月氷雪中拈出青絹扇子。者僧若再進後語，敢保老漢別有語在。上堂：謝景德、王溪長老并因藏主破砂盆，無貴賤，等閑拈向昌江上，盡大地人同一見。見

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 上堂。魚行水濁，鳥飛毛落。

Senses.Explanation: A fish stirs the water; a bird sheds a feather is a paired saying about the visible trace left by movement. Poshan replies with the pair when asked what a teacher’s relic does on entering a stupa. Dabo opens an address with it, then says an alert guest can recognize fire from smoke. Lianyue uses it after asking how a teacher serves people. Yikui gives it as his answer to a question about shared true knowledge. Huiyue gives it in reply to a donor’s question about a requested teaching. Liaozong places it after contrasting two readings of appearances, while Yuejian puts it beside a warning that even a tiny fixed view is a mistake.

Senses.Note: Three late masters actively reuse the same fixed image; the Ryukyu witness is an authored dedication verse, not the dedicatee’s speech.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB359.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baiyu. Baiyu Jingsi includes fish leaping and kites flying in a list and rejects simply identifying that list with the patriarchal mind.

Senses.Explanation: “Fish leap, kites fly” is a paired image of lively motion in water and sky. Baiyu Jingsi places the pair beside stars racing, lightning curling, flame passing wind, and a torrent crossing a blade in a retreat-release address. Zhe'an Jingfan says that, once feet are released, fish leaping and kites flying are companions of the way. In an authored gatha for the king of Zhongshan in Ryukyu, Weilin Daopei places the pair between birds and flowers disclosing their activity and the Great Way returning. Baiyu also includes it among rain falling, sun shining, water flowing, and birds calling, then rejects simply naming that list the patriarchal mind. The phrase supplies a lively two-level image, while each address decides what may or may not be said with it.

AlternateTargets: a tiny graphic difference causing a wrong reading
Senses.Note: The saying names scribal or visual confusion between similar graphs and commonly travels with the knife-graph comparison; Chan speakers use it for near resemblance that masks a consequential error.

Senses.Explanation: Confusing “fish” with “Lu” is mistaking one similar-looking written graph for another, a small visual slip that changes what is read. Gulin transmits Xuedou’s textual warning, Liao’an applies the pair to mistaken recognition, Poshan reverses its order while revising a ranking, and Xueyan applies it to uneven command hidden by fluent talk.
